name: Editing Supplements Value
use_when: The edit is accumulating effects, SFX, captions, or memes faster than it is adding clarity.
A video has weak retention and the editor needs to decide whether the problem is editing or core value.
A creator wants high-energy editing without losing trust.
A Resolve editor is spending too long rebuilding effects instead of using reusable presets.
An After Effects editor is building a complex Reel and needs every asset/effect to serve the message.
A viral-style YouTube edit risks adding every available effect instead of supporting the script.
A human short-form story works better as a lightly edited but carefully thought-through cut.
avoid_when: The format explicitly depends on maximalist style and the target audience expects it.
A dense effect stack is part of a deliberate comedy, gaming, anime, or music-video grammar.
The user asks for a style-pack test rather than final editorial judgment.

timeline_pattern.value_rule: Editing should supplement the value; it should not become the main reason a weak idea exists.
timeline_pattern.one_focus_rule: At any moment, the viewer should know what to watch, hear, or read.
timeline_pattern.idea_rule: If the idea is not interesting to the target viewer, polishing can only improve the packaging, not the core demand.
timeline_pattern.efficiency_rule: For high-volume short-form work, reusable presets, templates, and Power Bins can be more professional than rebuilding flashy effects for hours.
timeline_pattern.style_rule: A style system is a foundation for creativity, not a reason to repeat the same edit lazily.
timeline_pattern.space_rule: Do not cut every pause by default; keep space when it makes the story, joke, tension, or comprehension stronger.
timeline_pattern.imperfection_rule: Keep imperfect human texture when it creates connection, but trim it once the connection beat has landed.
timeline_pattern.iteration_rule: Learn one useful new technique per project, but do not let learning turn the edit into an endless perfection loop.

motion.rule: Remove shakes, zooms, wipes, and overlays that do not guide attention, clarify meaning, or create intentional style.
motion.slow_human_note: A simple dynamic zoom or proof insert can be stronger than forcing new effects into every long section.

sound.rule: Remove repeated whooshes or meme SFX that do not sell a real beat.

captions.rule: Captions should clarify speech or emphasize meaning; they should not create a second competing script.

color.rule: Stylized color is useful only when it supports tone and readability.

implementation.ffmpeg: Create a no-effects or low-effects review export of a problem section and compare clarity against the polished version.
implementation.remotion: Give optional effects a purpose label and disable effects whose purpose is empty or redundant.
implementation.blender: Keep animated flourishes modular so they can be removed without damaging the main edit.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Toggle effect stacks off, review whether the story still works, then restore only the effects with a clear job.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use adjustment-layer toggles and duplicate sequences to compare clean, moderate, and maximal versions. In After Effects, toggle heavy effects/textures and ask whether each layer clarifies the segment. In Resolve, compare simple cut, Fusion polish, and Power Bin preset versions.

common_mistakes: Mistaking editor effort for viewer value.
Using upbeat music or effects to hide slow pacing instead of fixing the cut.
Keeping a visual joke that distracts from the promise.
Adding several attention devices at once when one focal guide would be clearer.
Spending ten hours on a short when a reusable checked preset would produce consistent quality faster.
Adding assets to the screen only because the editor wants the frame to look advanced.
Assuming a minimally edited human story is weak because it has fewer visible effects.
Cutting meaningful space because the editor assumes every millisecond must move fast.
Treating every possible improvement as a blocker to publishing.
qc: Can every effect be named by its job?
Does the edit still make sense with effects temporarily disabled?
Is there only one primary focus at each moment?
Does music enhance the pacing rather than hide a slow cut?
Is the core video idea strong enough for the target viewer?
Could a checked preset or reusable style produce the same quality faster?
Does every After Effects layer have a message, focus, transition, or brand job?
Are pauses removed only when they are truly dead air?
Are kept imperfections adding connection rather than merely leaving mistakes in the cut?
Are remaining improvements optional rather than blocking?
